1,920 likes, 94 comments - anoushkalila on October 30, 2026: "I can’t think there are many places in the world that can be as equally compelling in early morning mists as it is in bright sunshine as @naturhotelforsthofgut (ad pr), an alpine retreat in the Austrian mountains.

The first port of call on our annual Autumn road trip adventure, Naturhotel Forsthofgut was the perfect easing in to our trip. We briefly contemplated the outdoor activities on offer (of which there are many), before promptly trading in our hiking boots for sauna sessions, languid meals across the hotel’s numerous restaurants, and petting the resident donkeys and ponies. 

If you’re looking for a family friendly stay, I could not recommend it more. I honestly found myself kind of wishing I could be a kid here again, to experience riding horses, paddle board in the pond, and getting creative in the art centre with the enthusiasm of youth. But it’s just as much a haven for us adults - between sauna hopping, sunbathing, and dining very, very well, we were kept more than happily occupied.".

2,468 likes, 72 comments - anoushkalila on October 28, 2026: "I am largely not a hiking holiday sort of person. I tend to gravitate to cities, culture, a good food scene and a nice boutique hotel. But this trip was all about Autumn colours, long walks, and immersing ourselves in nature, and it was, both literally and metaphorically, a breath of fresh air. 

Lake Gosausee in Austria was one of the main highlights of our itinerary, and we happily timed it just as the hills that surround it turned a fierce red, and the mountains were fringed with the first snow. 

Unfortunately the weather was not quite so fortuitous, and we set off on the hike between Vorderer and Hinterer Gosausee (a larger and smaller lake, connected by forest) under rainy grey skies. 

Thankfully by the time we made it to Hinterer Gosausee, the rain ceased and we were met with dramatic vistas. And by the time we hiked back to Vorderer Gousasee, we were even treated to hints of sun. 

It isn’t an easy hike, with some trialing uphills on the way out. But the views (and sense of satisfaction when you make it to the lake) are well worth it. Finish with a well earned hot chocolate at the end, and it’s a rather lovely Autumn day out.".

24K likes, 246 comments - anoushkalila on October 26, 2026: "24 hours in Hallstatt in its Autumn finery 🍂

We hadn’t initially planned on visiting Hallstatt on our Autumn Austrian road trip. But when I realised we were going to be a mere 15 minute drive away, it seemed silly not to spend a night.

Last time we visited Hallstatt, on a briskly cold December morning, we travelled through the night across country from Vienna to make it for sunrise. This time, we stayed in the centre of town, and our commute to the famous Hallstatt postcard view (photo 2) was but a mere 5 minute stroll. We were met by a sea of tripods, so promptly decided to sack it off and explore the quieter corners of the town, as evidenced by these snaps. 

I have mixed feelings about Hallstatt. It is extremely photogenic, fairytale-worthy, but so are 100 other towns in the vicinity, and past about 10am it becomes claustrophobic.  If you’re exploring this part of Austria, it’s well worth seeing - and then getting out to some of the quieter alpine towns and other beautiful lakes around the region.

Oh, and if you have a car? Drive just 20 minutes out of town for lunch at Rathlucken Hütte. It’s cash only, with a beautiful garden terrace and gorgeous mountain views on the drive up. Save space for the kaiserschmarrn!".

2,415 likes, 66 comments - anoushkalila on October 18, 2026: "Another set from Český Krumlov, because I haven’t had time to edit anything else lately. It’s been a non-stop few weeks (I write this at 03:58, willing my morning coffee to give me the energy to tackle an obnoxiously early flight), so I hope you’ll forgive me the brief radio silence. 

Anyway, Český Krumlov. I’ve already waxed lyrical about this charming Czech town (I even have a guide, which you can discover in my last post), and yet I still somehow have more to share.

This was our first morning, again horribly early, when the view from the castle was a sea of rooftops and smoking chimneys in the first golden glow of dawn. If you’re visiting Český Krumlov, I highly recommend making it up to the castle for either sunrise or sunset - both are beautiful. It’s also the quietest time to take in the view, as many of the tourists who make up the crowds here are day trippers from Prague. 

Today we’re actually flying to somewhere pretty close by, hopefully just in time for a sea of Autumn colours. I’ve packed my chunkiest knits, brand new hiking boots, and a bajillion lenses, give or take…".

2,138 likes, 89 comments - anoushkalila on October 9, 2026: "Comment “GUIDE” to get my free Český Krumlov guide straight to your inbox, with all my top tips for sightseeing, spectacular views, and the best dining 👇🏼

Considering we only had a day in Český Krumlov, we managed to take so many pictures that I’m probably going to be bombarding you for years to come. But when it looks like this, can you blame me?

I expected this beautiful Czech fairytale town to be picturesque, but I didn’t expect there to be quite so much to do. The town has a thriving arts and culture scene, and centuries of rich history. So yes, there’s truly breathtaking vistas. But there’s also so much beneath the surface.

My Český Krumlov cheat sheet:

- Visit the Castle Museum and Tower, Egon Schiele Art Centrum (we fell in love with the beautiful work of Lois Fasching on display here), Monastery Museum and Museum Fotoatelier Seidel
- Brunch at Bistro Topinka, dinner at Krčma Šatlava
- Grab a cocktail at Apotheka after a day of exploring
- Head to the viewpoints in and around the tower complex for sunset
- 30 minutes outside Český Krumlov Hluboká Castle makes a great half day trip

Lots more tips on where to stay and what to do over on the blog - I so hope it’s helpful. My outfit is also fully shoppable - link in bio!

4,331 likes, 89 comments - anoushkalila on October 7, 2026: "There is no such thing as a quiet hour in Prague. Even at the crack of dawn Charles Bridge is a hive of activity, and the crowds at the Astronomical Clock converge long before the first morning coffee is drunk. Our usual preference for empty shots was a non-starter, and we ended up with all sorts of random slivers of footage with no cohesive tone or story.

Whilst I love editing photographs, I’ll admit I find video a chore. So I decided to try and mix it up with this one, and have a bit of fun with it. It’s a bit scrappy, but I’ve tried to convey some of the essence of the city. The imposing statues and sculptures of Prague Castle’s grand St. Vitus Cathedral. An analogue photo booth in an unassuming shopping complex hidden in a backstreet. And the trams that make traversing the city oh so aesthetic.

I guess this is a bit of a love letter to Prague, a city I hate to shoot but love to explore. I have lots more practical tips and recommendations for this city coming soon too, so follow along if you’re planning a trip.".

13K likes, 136 comments - anoushkalila on September 18, 2026: "Frames from The Pink House on Loch Glass, Scotland. 

We were meant to be heading to our hotel on the East Coast after a horribly early airport start, when I spotted this house during a quick Google Maps peruse of the route. A quick detour, a 40 minute hike, a few good dog encounters later (my day immediately becomes at least 50% better if I get to pet a dog) and we were exploring the beautiful Loch Glass, where this eery, abandoned, and rather Barbie coded house sits. 

A Scotland road trip has become somewhat of a yearly pilgrimage for us, and its places like this that keep us coming back. It’s dramatic, sometimes desolate beauty. The freshness of the Highland air. Oh, and the promise of a full Scottish, of course (hold the black pudding, but I will absolutely have some haggis).

15K likes, 143 comments - anoushkalila on September 25, 2026: "The most beautiful place in England at the most beautiful time of year 🍂

On paper, I feel I should hate The Cotswolds. It’s touristy, it’s busy, it’s extremely hyped, it’s expensive (looking at you, Daylesford). And yet, it is simply so wonderfully pretty that all those things cease to matter. Particularly in Autumn (okay I squeezed in a couple of Spring snaps too, but shhh, don’t tell), when the leaves turn brown and the ivy glows red, it is a visual feast. And getting all cosy next to a roaring pub fire with a Sunday roast and all the trimmings? About as perfect as it gets. 

If you’re planning a Cotswolds trip, here’s a shortlist of the towns and villages I’d recommend putting on your itinerary:

- Castle Combe 
- Bibury
- Lower Slaughter 
- Chipping Campden 
- Bourton-on-the-water 
- Stow-on-the-Wold
- Burford
- Snowshill 
- Tetbury
- Painswick
- Broadway

A quick Autumnal Cotswolds 101

- The best time to go to see Autumn colour is usually the end of October and beginning of November, however this can vary year by year depending on the climate
- It’s doable by public transport, but I’d recommend driving if you can
- Stay in local village B&Bs, or book a stay at the Cluedo Manor-worthy @themanor_house 
- Combine with a trip to nearby Bath, Bristol, or Oxford
- If you do one thing, make it a classic Sunday pub roast 

Autumn in the Cotswolds | Fall in England | Autumn Destinations in England | UK in Fall | Prettiest Cotswolds Villages | Cotswolds Travel | UK Travel Destinations".

2,226 likes, 89 comments - anoushkalila on September 22, 2026: "I’ll be honest, before my most recent India trip I’d never given Delhi much time of day. It was usually just a gateway to Rajasthan, a brief stopover to get over my jet lag. On first glance, it fits all of the worst stereotypes that exist about India - crowded, loud, dirty. 

But on this trip, we actually made an effort to brush off the jet lag and see some of the city. And for the first time, I found myself actually understanding Delhi’s appeal. It has some wonderful sights, most notably the Qutub Minar which is the first image in this series. At sunrise, we had the place all to ourselves in the most beautiful morning glow, whilst a friendly security guard showed us some of the best photo spots. 

For golden hour, we headed back out to Humayun’s Tomb. It was busy, but not unpleasantly so. If anything, the atmosphere felt almost festive, with tourists from all over India converging to explore this spectacular monument. 

A moment, also, for our hotel, @theleelapalacenewdelhi. I genuinely don’t think I could visit Delhi and stay anywhere else now. The service was pristine, and we ate some of the best curries we’ve had there. 

So next time I’m in India, I’m going to make sure to give Delhi at least a couple of days. Beneath the surface, it’s really rather charming.

954 likes, 56 comments - anoushkalila on October 3, 2026: "As many of you will know, much of our travel is dictated by the places the England men’s football team play. So when England were scheduled to play Czechia in Prague, we immediately booked our flights. Except the ticket allocation was decidedly lower than usual, and we came out of the ballot empty handed.

So what to do with flights to Prague, and no football? Well, a short side quest to Český Krumlov seemed as good an answer as any. I knew next to nothing about this South Bohemian town before visiting, and had left most of the planning to Adam. It seemed like a fun excursion, if little else.

We arrived just as the sun was setting (and if you’ve watched to the end of this video, you’ll know it’s a pretty spectacular sunset). The town felt positively festive, with glowing taverns and a bustling market square, where traditional folk dancers performed as visitors tucked into local delicacies. 

The next morning we got up at the crack of dawn to explore. This was hard work at the time (the 5:30am alarm was not pleasant), but a decision we fully stood by once we saw just how many coach parties rolled in not long after. 

We headed up to the castle to watch the town slowly wake, greeted by panoramic views of church spires and puffing chimneys, sinuously circled by the Vltava river.  It was a view that made the lack of tickets, two hour drive, and early start all worth it. 

I’m working on a full guide to Český Krumlov, as the town is so much more than just pretty views. If you have anything you’d like to see in it, please do pop a comment down below.".

The town felt positively festive, with glowing taverns and a bustling market square, where traditional folk dancers performed as visitors tucked into local delicacies. 

The next morning we got up at the crack of dawn to explore. This was hard work at the time (the 5:30am alarm was not pleasant), but a decision we fully stood by once we saw just how many coach parties rolled in not long after. 

We headed up to the castle to watch the town slowly wake, greeted by panoramic views of church spires and puffing chimneys, sinuously circled by the Vltava river.  It was a view that made the lack of tickets, two hour drive, and early start all worth it. 

I’m working on a full guide to Český Krumlov, as the town is so much more than just pretty views. If you have anything you’d like to see in it, please do pop a comment down below.".
